knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221109)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Wang_2022_abrocitinib_QTcF")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpdd.1111>

Wang et al. (2022) analysed the thorough-QT study of abrocitinib, a selective
Janus kinase 1 inhibitor for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. Healthy
volunteers received single oral doses of abrocitinib 600 mg, placebo and
moxifloxacin 400 mg in a randomized three-period crossover. Two prespecified
linear mixed-effects models related the time-matched abrocitinib plasma
concentration to the change from baseline in the Fridericia-corrected QT
interval (DeltaQTcF) and in heart rate (DeltaHR). The package carries one file
for each:

| Model file | Endpoint | Output | Source table |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Wang_2022_abrocitinib_QTcF` | DeltaQTcF (ms) | `QTcF` | Table 1 |
| `Wang_2022_abrocitinib_HR` | DeltaHR (bpm) | `d_hr` | Table 2 |

Both models share one structure (Wang 2022 Equations 1 and 3):

$$
\Delta Y_{ijk} = (\theta_0 + \eta_{0,i}) + (\theta_1 + \eta_{1,i})\,C_{ijk}
  + \theta_2\,\mathrm{TRT} + \theta_3\,(Y_{ij0} - \bar{Y}_0) + \theta_k + \varepsilon_{ijk}
$$

where `TRT` is 0 in the placebo period and 1 in the abrocitinib period
(`ON_TREATMENT`), `C` is the abrocitinib plasma concentration
(`CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML`, 0 for placebo), `Y_ij0` is the period baseline
(`QTC_BL` or `HR`) and `theta_k` is a free intercept shift for each nominal
post-dose time other than the first (`NTIME`, reference 0.25 h). Both random
effects are additive and correlated. The time-matched placebo-corrected effect
used for the regulatory assessment is therefore

$$
\Delta\Delta Y = \theta_2 + \theta_1\,C .
$$

Both are PD-only models: concentrations enter as data. To simulate from a
dose, this vignette drives them with the registry's abrocitinib population PK
model, `Wojciechowski_2022_abrocitinib` (Wojciechowski 2022, the population PK
analysis cited by Wang 2022 for the atopic-dermatitis Cmax).

# Population

Thirty-six healthy adults (31 White, 3 Black, 2 other) were randomized; mean
age 33.2 years (range 19-55), mean weight 80.2 kg (range 55.8-105.4), mean body
mass index 24.7 kg/m^2 (Wang 2022 Results). The sex distribution is not
reported. Mean baseline heart rate was 54.1-54.7 bpm and mean baseline QTcF
399.2-400.7 ms across the treatment groups. Triplicate ECGs were recorded at
-1, -0.5 and 0 h before and at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 and 24 h after each
dose, with a PK sample at each post-dose ECG time. A total of 864
observations entered the concentration-QTc analysis; moxifloxacin data were
used only to show assay sensitivity.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Model structure (both endpoints) | linear mixed-effects, Eq. 1 / Eq. 3 | Methods |
| QTcF `e0` (theta0) | -0.0062 ms | Table 1 |

| QTcF `e_on_treatment_e0` (theta2) | 0.3141 ms | Table 1 |
| QTcF `e_qtc_bl_e0` (theta3) | -0.0577 ms/ms | Table 1 |
| QTcF `e_ntime0p5_e0` ... `e_ntime24_e0` (theta4-theta10) | -2.678, -1.851, -3.152, -2.666, -7.052, -3.402, -5.103 ms | Table 1 |

# Models

```{r models}
mod_qtcf <- readModelDb("Wang_2022_abrocitinib_QTcF")
mod_hr <- readModelDb("Wang_2022_abrocitinib_HR")

# Typical-value forms. `omega = NA` is also passed at each typical-value
# rxSolve() so that no etas are re-sampled from options retained by the
# compiled model.
mod_qtcf_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_qtcf)
mod_hr_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_hr)

ntime_levels <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 24)

# Event table for the PD-only models. There are no dosing records and no ODE
# states; every covariate is a column. The models are algebraic, so the rows
# can share one id with arbitrary increasing times.
pd_events <- function(conc, on_trt, ntime, qtc_bl = 400, hr_bl = 54.4) {
  n <- max(length(conc), length(on_trt), length(ntime))
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = seq_len(n), evid = 0L, amt = 0,
    CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML = rep_len(conc, n),
    ON_TREATMENT = rep_len(on_trt, n),
    NTIME = rep_len(ntime, n),
    QTC_BL = qtc_bl, HR = hr_bl
  )
}

solve_typ <- function(model, ev) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, omega = NA))
}
```

# Structural checks

At zero concentration, in the placebo period and at the mean baseline, each
model must return exactly `e0` at the 0.25 h reference and `e0 + theta_k` at
every other nominal time. These are identities of the encoding, so they are
asserted at machine precision. They also confirm that the nominal-time binning
selects the intended level and that no random effect leaked into the
typical-value solve.

```{r structural-ntime}
ev <- pd_events(conc = 0, on_trt = 0, ntime = ntime_levels)
chk_ntime <- data.frame(
  NTIME = ntime_levels,
  QTcF = solve_typ(mod_qtcf_typ, ev)$QTcF,
  d_hr = solve_typ(mod_hr_typ, ev)$d_hr
)
expected_qtcf <- -0.0062 +
  c(0, -2.678, -1.851, -3.152, -2.666, -7.052, -3.402, -5.103)
expected_hr <- -0.669 +
  c(0, 0.0797, -0.299, -0.7794, -0.5218, 5.689, 4.274, 3.111)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(chk_ntime$QTcF, expected_qtcf, tolerance = 1e-12)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(chk_ntime$d_hr, expected_hr, tolerance = 1e-12))
)

chk_ntime |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Nominal time (h)" = NTIME,
    "Placebo DeltaQTcF (ms)" = QTcF,
    "Placebo DeltaHR (bpm)" = d_hr
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical placebo-period prediction at each nominal time (zero concentration, mean baseline).")
```

The diurnal pattern of the nominal-time effects differs between the endpoints:
QTcF is lowest 6 h after dosing, while heart rate rises by 4-6 bpm from 6 h
onwards. These shifts are common to both periods and cancel in the
placebo-corrected contrast.

# Placebo-corrected effect at the supratherapeutic concentration (Table 3)

Wang 2022 Table 3 reports the model-predicted mean time-matched
placebo-corrected change from baseline at the concentration quoted for healthy
volunteers (1701 ng/mL) and at the supratherapeutic concentration in atopic
dermatitis (2156 ng/mL: the predicted 200 mg once-daily steady-state Cmax of
1123 ng/mL times the 1.92-fold increase under fluconazole). The model
reproduces it as the difference between an abrocitinib-period prediction at
concentration `C` and a placebo-period prediction at zero concentration, at the
same nominal time and baseline. The check is run at every nominal time and at
off-mean baselines, because all other terms must cancel.

```{r table3}
ddelta <- function(model_typ, out, conc, ntime, qtc_bl = 400, hr_bl = 54.4) {
  act <- solve_typ(model_typ, pd_events(conc, 1, ntime, qtc_bl, hr_bl))[[out]]
  pbo <- solve_typ(model_typ, pd_events(0, 0, ntime, qtc_bl, hr_bl))[[out]]
  act - pbo
}

conc_tab3 <- c(1701, 2156)
tab3 <- data.frame(
  Population = c("Healthy volunteers", "Patients with AD"),
  conc = conc_tab3,
  qtcf_pub = c(4.8, 6.00),
  qtcf_sim = ddelta(mod_qtcf_typ, "QTcF", conc_tab3, ntime = 1),
  hr_pub = c(5.1, 6.51),
  hr_sim = ddelta(mod_hr_typ, "d_hr", conc_tab3, ntime = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    qtcf_pct = 100 * (qtcf_sim - qtcf_pub) / qtcf_pub,
    hr_pct = 100 * (hr_sim - hr_pub) / hr_pub
  )

# The contrast must not depend on the nominal time or the baseline.
grid <- expand.grid(ntime = ntime_levels, qtc_bl = c(380, 420), hr_bl = c(45, 65))
spread <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
  q <- ddelta(mod_qtcf_typ, "QTcF", 2156, grid$ntime[i], grid$qtc_bl[i], grid$hr_bl[i])
  h <- ddelta(mod_hr_typ, "d_hr", 2156, grid$ntime[i], grid$qtc_bl[i], grid$hr_bl[i])
  max(abs(q - tab3$qtcf_sim[2]), abs(h - tab3$hr_sim[2]))
}, numeric(1))

stopifnot(
  max(spread) < 1e-10,
  # Exact identity with the closed form theta2 + theta1 * C
  isTRUE(all.equal(tab3$qtcf_sim, 0.3141 + 0.0026 * conc_tab3, tolerance = 1e-12)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(tab3$hr_sim, -0.1979 + 0.0031 * conc_tab3, tolerance = 1e-12)),
  # Against the published means; the residual gap is the 2-significant-figure
  # rounding of the printed slopes (see below).
  all(abs(tab3$qtcf_pct) < 3),
  all(abs(tab3$hr_pct) < 3)
)

tab3 |>
  dplyr::select(Population, conc, qtcf_pub, qtcf_sim, qtcf_pct, hr_pub, hr_sim, hr_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Concentration (ng/mL)" = conc,
    "DeltaDeltaQTcF published (ms)" = qtcf_pub,
    "DeltaDeltaQTcF model (ms)" = qtcf_sim,
    "QTcF % diff" = qtcf_pct,
    "DeltaDeltaHR published (bpm)" = hr_pub,
    "DeltaDeltaHR model (bpm)" = hr_sim,
    "HR % diff" = hr_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Wang 2022 (mean placebo-corrected effects).")
```

The model reproduces the published means within 1.3% (QTcF) and 0.5% (HR). The
gap is the rounding of the printed slopes: solving Table 3 for the QTcF slope,
`(6.00 - 0.3141) / 2156` and `(4.8 - 0.3141) / 1701` both give 0.00264
ms/(ng/mL), which Table 1 prints as 0.0026. The model keeps the printed value.
The 90% confidence intervals of Table 3 cannot be reproduced because they
depend on the sampling covariance of theta1 and theta2, which is not reported.

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Typical placebo-corrected effect across the studied concentration range. Replicates the mean lines of Figures 4 and 5 of Wang 2022; the dashed vertical line is the 2156 ng/mL supratherapeutic concentration and the dotted horizontal line the 10 ms / 10 bpm threshold."}
conc_grid <- seq(0, 4500, by = 50)
curve_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(endpoint = "DeltaDeltaQTcF (ms)", conc = conc_grid,
             value = ddelta(mod_qtcf_typ, "QTcF", conc_grid, ntime = 1)),
  data.frame(endpoint = "DeltaDeltaHR (bpm)", conc = conc_grid,
             value = ddelta(mod_hr_typ, "d_hr", conc_grid, ntime = 1))
)
ggplot(curve_df, aes(conc, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2156, linetype = "dashed", colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dotted", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  labs(x = "Abrocitinib concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Placebo-corrected change from baseline") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Driving the models from a dose

The PD models need an abrocitinib concentration at each ECG time. Here they
come from `Wojciechowski_2022_abrocitinib` for a single 600 mg dose in healthy
adults. The formulation of the thorough-QT tablets is not stated; the
commercial (phase III) tablet is assumed. Covariates follow the reported
demographics: weight drawn from a normal distribution with the reported mean
and truncated at the reported range, 2 of 36 subjects (5.6%) of other race,
and all subjects male because the sex split is not reported.

```{r pk-sim, message = FALSE}
n_sub <- 120
pk_mod <- readModelDb("Wojciechowski_2022_abrocitinib")

set.seed(20221109)
wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 80.2, 12), 55.8), 105.4)
cov_df <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub), WT = wt, SEXF = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0,
  RACE_OTHER = as.integer(seq_len(n_sub) %% 18 == 0),
  ADOLESCENT = 0, DIS_PSORIASIS = 0, DIS_ATOPIC_DERMATITIS = 0,
  HEPIMP_MILD = 0, HEPIMP_MOD = 0,
  CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 0, CONMED_FLUCONAZOLE = 0, CONMED_FLUVOXAMINE = 0,
  FED_HIGHFAT = 0, FORM_ABROCITINIB_SUSP = 0, FORM_ABROCITINIB_TAB_PH2B = 0,
  FORM_ABROCITINIB_TAB_PH3 = 1, MULTI_DOSE = 0,
  DOSE_ABROCITINIB_MG = 600, DOSE_ABROCITINIB_MGD = 600,
  STUDY_B7451005 = 0, STUDY_B7451006 = 0, STUDY_B7451012 = 0,
  STUDY_B7451043 = 0
)

# Dense grid for NCA plus the nominal ECG times; each dose is a depot record
# and a rate = -1 central record (see the Wojciechowski 2022 vignette).
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.25, 4, by = 0.25), 5:12, 16, 20, 24, ntime_levels)))
pk_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = 0, amt = 600, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = 0),
  data.frame(time = 0, amt = 600, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", rate = -1),
  data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
)
pk_events <- merge(cov_df, pk_events, by = NULL) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, rate, dplyr::everything()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

pk_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(pk_mod, events = pk_events, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "abrocitinib 600 mg")
```

## PKNCA on the driving concentrations

```{r pknca}
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  pk_sim |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)),
  Cc ~ time | treatment + id
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = 0, amt = 600, treatment = "abrocitinib 600 mg"),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    geomean = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))),
    median = stats::median(PPORRES),
    p05 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    p95 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(nca_summary, digits = 2, caption = "NCA of the simulated 600 mg single-dose profiles (0-24 h).")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = data.frame(treatment = "abrocitinib 600 mg", cmax = 1701),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median Cmax against the 1701 ng/mL healthy-volunteer concentration of Wang 2022 Table 3.")
```

Wang 2022 does not report NCA for this study. The exposure information it
gives is the 1701 ng/mL quoted for healthy volunteers in Table 3, a maximum
observed concentration above 4000 ng/mL, and the mean concentration-time
profile of Figure 3c, which peaks at the 3 h sample. The simulated Tmax of
2.75 h is the end of the zero-order absorption arm that the PK model applies to
doses above 121 mg, which is why it is the same in every subject. The
comparison is a plausibility check of the PK driver, not a test of the QTc
models: the upstream PK model was fitted to other studies, and its formulation
and sex inputs here are assumptions.

```{r fig3c, fig.cap = "Simulated mean (90% CI) concentration at the nominal ECG times against the observed means of Figure 3c of Wang 2022 (red; read from the figure by the maintainers, approximate)."}
# Approximate means read from Wang 2022 Figure 3c (ng/mL).
fig3c_obs <- data.frame(
  time = ntime_levels,
  conc = c(240, 810, 1140, 1510, 1950, 1030, 270, 70)
)
pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% ntime_levels) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(Cc),
    lo = mean - stats::qt(0.95, dplyr::n() - 1) * stats::sd(Cc) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    hi = mean + stats::qt(0.95, dplyr::n() - 1) * stats::sd(Cc) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, mean)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = fig3c_obs, aes(time, conc), colour = "firebrick", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Abrocitinib concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Simulated crossover

Each simulated subject contributes an abrocitinib period (concentration from
the PK simulation at each nominal ECG time) and a placebo period
(concentration 0), with one set of random effects per subject as in the
source model. Baseline QTcF and HR are drawn from normal distributions
centred on the reported means; their spreads (SD 15 ms and 7 bpm) are
assumptions because the paper reports only the means.

```{r pd-sim}
pd_cov <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  QTC_BL = rnorm(n_sub, 400, 15),
  HR = rnorm(n_sub, 54.4, 7)
)
conc_at_ecg <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% ntime_levels) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, NTIME = time, CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML = Cc)

pd_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_at_ecg |> dplyr::mutate(ON_TREATMENT = 1, period = "abrocitinib", time = NTIME),
  conc_at_ecg |> dplyr::mutate(ON_TREATMENT = 0, period = "placebo", time = 100 + NTIME,
                               CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pd_cov, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, dplyr::everything()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

sim_qtcf <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_qtcf, events = pd_ev, keep = c("period", "NTIME", "CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML")))
sim_hr <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hr, events = pd_ev, keep = c("period", "NTIME", "CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML")))

pd_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_qtcf |> dplyr::transmute(id, period, NTIME, conc = CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML,
                               endpoint = "QTcF (ms)", value = sim),
  sim_hr |> dplyr::transmute(id, period, NTIME, conc = CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML,
                             endpoint = "HR (bpm)", value = sim)
)

# Time-matched placebo correction within subject
pd_dd <- pd_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(id, NTIME, endpoint), names_from = period, values_from = c(value, conc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ddelta = value_abrocitinib - value_placebo, conc = conc_abrocitinib)
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Simulated change from baseline against abrocitinib concentration in the abrocitinib period with a linear fit. Replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Wang 2022."}
pd_long |>
  dplyr::filter(period == "abrocitinib") |>
  ggplot(aes(conc, value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Abrocitinib concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Change from baseline") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Mean (90% CI) simulated placebo-corrected change from baseline and mean concentration over time. Replicates Figure 3 of Wang 2022: the effect peaks with the concentration, with no delay."}
fig3_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pd_dd |> dplyr::transmute(NTIME, panel = paste0("DeltaDelta", endpoint), y = ddelta),
  conc_at_ecg |> dplyr::transmute(NTIME, panel = "Concentration (ng/mL)", y = CP_ABROCITINIB_NGML)
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel, NTIME) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(y),
    lo = mean - stats::qt(0.95, dplyr::n() - 1) * stats::sd(y) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    hi = mean + stats::qt(0.95, dplyr::n() - 1) * stats::sd(y) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(fig3_df, aes(NTIME, mean)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Nominal time after dose (h)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Regressing the simulated placebo-corrected effects on concentration should
recover the model slopes, because the nominal-time and baseline terms cancel
within subject. The regression slope is compared with the model slope with a
tolerance of 30%: several standard errors wide for 120 subjects (realised
differences are about 3-10%), while a mis-transcribed slope or a unit error
moves it by far more.

```{r slope-gate}
fit_slopes <- pd_dd |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    slope_hat = unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(ddelta ~ conc))[2]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    slope_model = ifelse(endpoint == "QTcF (ms)", 0.0026, 0.0031),
    pct_diff = 100 * (slope_hat - slope_model) / slope_model
  )
stopifnot(all(abs(fit_slopes$pct_diff) < 30))
fit_slopes |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint,
    "Regression slope (per ng/mL)" = slope_hat,
    "Model slope (per ng/mL)" = slope_model,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5, caption = "Slope of simulated placebo-corrected effect on concentration.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Centering constants.** The models centre baseline QTcF and HR on "the
  overall mean of all the baseline values", which the paper does not print.
  The rounded values 400 ms and 54.4 bpm sit inside the reported ranges of
  treatment-group means (399.2-400.7 ms and 54.1-54.7 bpm); the resulting
  error in any prediction is below 0.05 ms or 0.05 bpm.
* **Nominal-time reference.** The reference level is the first post-dose time,
  0.25 h, as stated for theta0 ("placebo, at the first postdose sampling
  time"). `NTIME` is binned to the nearest scheduled level inside the model, so
  a value between grid points is assigned to the closest one.
* **Treatment indicator in a crossover.** `ON_TREATMENT` is constant within a
  period and changes between periods. Each subject has one intercept and one
  slope random effect across periods, as in the source model.
* **Rounded slopes.** Table 1 prints the QTcF slope as 0.0026; Table 3 implies
  0.00264. The printed value is kept, which places the model 1.3% below the
  published DeltaDeltaQTcF means.
* **Correction-factor model not packaged.** Equation 2 (a log-log QT-RR model
  used to derive a study-specific correction) reports only its estimated
  exponent, 0.3375; Fridericia (0.333) was used for the primary analysis.
* **Upstream PK.** The concentration driver in this vignette is the separately
  published `Wojciechowski_2022_abrocitinib` model with an assumed commercial
  tablet formulation and all-male cohort; the QTc and HR models themselves were
  fitted to observed concentrations.
* **Figure 3c means.** The observed mean concentrations overlaid on the PK
  driver were read from Figure 3c by eye and are approximate; they are shown
  for comparison only and are not used by any assertion.
* **Baseline spreads.** The SDs of baseline QTcF and HR used in the simulated
  cohort are assumptions.
* **Metabolites.** The active metabolites M1 and M2 were not measured or
  modelled; the models describe parent abrocitinib only.
